stem.en: A cell with 8 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes does each daughter cell have?

text.en: 4, because the 8 chromosomes are shared between two cells.

feedback.en: This forgets the copy made before division.

text.en: 8, because each daughter gets a full set.

feedback.en: Yes. Mitosis keeps the number the same.

text.en: 16, because the DNA was copied before division.

feedback.en: The copies are shared out, one to each daughter cell.

text.en: 2, because each division takes away three quarters of them.

feedback.en: Mitosis does not reduce the number at all.

explanation.en: The cell copies its DNA first, and then one copy of each chromosome goes to each daughter cell. So each daughter cell has 8, the same as the parent.

hints.en: Compare the daughter cells with the parent cell.
